analysis.title: "Pnl Protection > Pnl Generation": Goldman Warns Still-Crowded Mag7 Is The Next "Source Of Funds"
key_insights: Goldman's Sharkey says the AI unwind is not finished. The desk net sold $4.2bn of tech on Friday, the most since the episode began, and finished the week as net sellers after fully reversing a mid-week buy skew of about $5bn.

October losses were concentrated in AI and TMT. The Nasdaq 100 had its worst month of underperformance vs the equal-weighted S&P since 2002, the SOX closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025, and TMT-focused hedge funds lost 11.9% in October.

Re-risking early in the week reversed after negative earnings reactions: INTC on PC weakness, AMZN on weak FCF and higher buyside AWS expectations, search weakness, and MSFT closing lower despite a beat. Goldman says this was deflating for investors who had just started to redeploy capital.

Prime book shows high gross and low net exposure. Overall gross leverage is 314.1% (97th percentile over five years) and net leverage is 73.6% (10th percentile over one year). The long/short ratio of 1.612 is at the 2nd percentile over five years.

De-grossing accelerated for a third straight week, with short covers outpacing long sales 1.8 to 1. Macro products (index and ETFs) made up 73% of net buying, so the global equity net buying was mostly hedges being covered.

Sharkey's conclusion is that 'pnl protection > pnl generation right now will limit offense being played in the near term (buyers live higher)'. Funds with YTD gains at risk are unlikely to buy dips until prices are higher.

Mag7 positioning has stayed resilient while the rest of AI was liquidated. Mag7 net exposure as a share of US Prime Book exposure rose from about 14% in June to about 22%, at the top of its five-year range. Goldman expects the group to act as a source of funds, limiting near-term dip buying demand.

Mag7 names were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions, which Goldman reads as little recovery in risk appetite. Sharkey's one wildcard is retail, where more volatility could bring more engagement and offset some weakness.
The S&P ex-AI had its best month since ChatGPT launched, up 7.64%, while the Mag7 fell roughly 4%, Goldman's broad AI basket fell roughly 14% and neoclouds fell roughly 36% (values read off a chart).

AI vs 'AI at Risk' (GSPUARTI) fell 25.7% in October, its second-worst month since ChatGPT launched. Goldman's Software vs Semis pair (GSPUSOSE) outperformed by 27%, the second-biggest monthly outperformance since 2015, and is up 88% from June lows.

Momentum was extremely volatile while the index went nowhere. Pasquariello gives monthly S&P returns of -0.13% (July), +2.62% (Aug), -0.45% (Sep), -0.93% (Oct) against GSPRHIMO at -30.19%, -13.67%, +26.96%, -18.60%.

Earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating. Q3 2026 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y, matching Q2, but the median stock is growing 12%, down from 14% in Q2. Cumulative Q3 EPS surprise is roughly 2pp twelve trading days into the season, about half the pace of Q2.

Defensives are at all-time highs: Berkshire, Coca-Cola, Philip Morris, AbbVie and Apple all hit records in the past two weeks while the Nasdaq 100 slid roughly 7%. The article cites BofA noting defensives were last this frothy at the dotcom peak.

Pasquariello's bull case: sentiment is 'unequivocally downbeat', the year-end seasonal swing is underway, and the market has cleared a significant amount of length. He concedes bears could say the same was said into late 2018.

Goldman's midterm trades: long ACA Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA) in a Democratic sweep, AI Power (GSENEPOW) over ex-Power AI hardware (GSTMTAIH), and corporate tax exposure (GSPUTAXP) on watch for beyond 2029. Brazil also saw its largest net selling in five years, driven by long sales.

The Zero Hedge author sides with Sharkey and expects the path of least resistance for the Mag7 to be lower until the crowded length is cleaned up, since the cap-weighted index cannot rally without them.

Weak FCF and higher buyside AWS expectations. Shares slid 7% on surging cash burn.
Jumped about 6% after hours on an Azure beat but closed in the red. Bookings and backlog were weaker.
Plunged on a top and bottom line miss. The article says Alphabet failed the reaction-to-the-reaction test.

sector_views.rationale: SOX closed below its 200-day moving average and is 27.1% below its June 22 high of 14,655. Goldman's Software vs Semis pair outperformed by 27% in October.
Software vs Semis pair is up 88% from June lows after 'AI will eat software' was consensus a year ago.
Coca-Cola, Philip Morris, AbbVie, Berkshire and Apple at all-time highs as money rotates out of AI.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 aggregate EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y (Goldman portfolio strategists, estimate for a season still in progress), matching Q2. Median stock EPS growth is 12% vs 14% in Q2.
Cumulative Q3 EPS surprise is roughly 2pp twelve trading days into the season (approximate, read off a chart), about half the pace of Q2 and barely above the average quarter since 2005.
INTC reported a negative EPS print on PC weakness and fell the most on record on Friday (reported results, week of Oct 26).
AMZN reported weak free cash flow and fell 7% on Friday on surging cash burn. Buyside expectations for AWS had been higher.
MSFT beat on Azure and rose about 6% after hours, but bookings and backlog were weaker and the stock closed lower.
GOOGL missed on both the top and bottom line and the stock plunged. The article also lists META and SpaceX as having failed the reaction-to-the-reaction test.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The index was flat over the quarter's months while momentum and AI baskets had large swings underneath.
Best month since ChatGPT launched, showing rotation away from AI names.
